title: kv-index-entropy-sleuth-and-hypotheses
content:
Summary:

This is a working notes doc capturing an unusual class of incidents where the KV index exhibits rapid changes in 'index entropy' (high churn of index buckets / hash collisions) which correlates with spikey eviction rates, transient host memory pressure, and periodic batch scheduling stalls. Behavior observed is different from a simple grow/shrink leak – it looks like index fragmentation + pathological access patterns cause hotspots + unexpected eviction oscillation which then amplifies batching latency.

Why this doc exists (context):
- Multiple SEV-level oncalls in Q3/Q4 reported short-lived (~1–5m) surges in host memory followed by immediate eviction storms and occasional deadlocks in the batch collector.
- Traditional metrics (host mem rss, kv-entries, eviction-rate) show correlation but not causation. New metric 'index_entropy' was instrumented to capture per-host distribution skew; high entropy correlates strongly with incidents.

Observed signals (quick checklist):
- index_entropy > 0.65 (cluster baseline ~0.12)
- per-bucket hit-rate variance spikes (stddev/hit_rate > 4x baseline)
- eviction_rate spikes to > 2000 ops/s for a host briefly
- continuous batching microbatch size drops to 1 or stalls for > 30s
- host free memory falls rapidly, then recovers as eviction completes
- request tail-latency percentiles (p99) jump 2–10x during window

Common immediate mitigation used in previous incidents (short-term):
- Redistribute tenants: kick low-priority host tenants to other hosts (eviction-cooldown window) to stop the oscillation.
- Increase eviction throttle temporarily (dynconfig) to smooth the rate and avoid lock contention.
- Disable prefetch for affected tenants to reduce write amplification into the index.
- If host is unstable, cordon + drain as last resort to prevent cross-host cascade.

Investigation steps (playbook sketch):
1) Triage and scope
   - Identify impacted hosts from alert (host list) and time window.
   - Query index_entropy timeseries for the window (grafana -> kv_index_entropy).
   - Check per-bucket histograms: grafana panel 'kv/index/bucket-histogram/<host>'
   - Correlate with eviction_rate, alloc_failures, and batch_collector_queue_length.

2) Quick forensics (logs + traces)
   - Pull serving-runtime logs for host: grep for "kv-index" and "bucket" markers.
   - Look for repeated rehash / grow / shrink cycles (log lines: "index.rehash.start" / "index.rehash.done").
   - Sample slow requests during window and dump KV hot keys: use debug endpoint /_debug/kv/hotkeys?host=<host>&window=60s.

3) Hypothesis scaffolding (what to test)
   - H1: Hash spread regression after model rollout changed access-patterns (new model prompts produce many distinct prefixes) -> index fragmentation.
   - H2: A recent change to the index resizing heuristic causes too-frequent rehashes under bursty workloads (concurrent rehash + eviction races).
   - H3: Prefetch misrouting created write amplification to a small subset of buckets leading to hot buckets and eviction thrash.
   - H4: Background async compaction/maintenance task starving batch collector threads due to priority inversion.

4) Experiments to validate hypotheses (quick wins)
   - For H1: correlate tenant/model ids with hotkey samples. If one tenant dominates, rollback model rollout or throttle that tenant.
   - For H2: temporarily raise resize threshold on one canary host (dynconfig) and see if index_entropy stabilizes.
   - For H3: toggle prefetch heuristic for the impacted shard (disable predictive prefetch) and check write amplification metrics.
   - For H4: profile thread cpu consumption (perf / pstack) and check maintenance task scheduling logs ("index.compaction" events).

Key commands / queries (SRE shell cheatsheet):
- Query entropy timeseries (promql): sum by (host) (rate(kv_index_entropy_bucket_count[2m])) / ignoring(bucket) group_left sum(rate(kv_index_total_buckets[2m]))
- Fetch hotkeys (debug api): curl -s "http://<host>:13000/_debug/kv/hotkeys?window=60s" | jq .
- Check logs: sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -o short-iso --since '2024-10-10T03:00:00' | rg "index.rehash|bucket|compact|prefetch" -n
- Force slow growth config (dynconfig): POST /dynconfig/hosts/<host>/kv_index_threshold {"min_load": 0.75} (ops team only)

Prior incidents & what we learned (summary):
- Incident 2024-07-19: index rehash thrash during a staged A/B rollout. Root cause: rollout increased unique prefix entropy by ~6x. Mitigation: immediate rollback + tenant throttling.
- Incident 2024-09-03: background compaction overlapped with eviction leading to lock convoy. Root cause: compaction priority lower than eviction, but both contend for same bucket locks. Mitigation: compaction backoff and stricter bucket-level lock release.

Proposed short-term fixes (actionable):
- Add a safeguard to avoid simultaneous rehash on >1 thread per host (mutex + backoff). Owner: Marcus Li. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Expose index_entropy to routing layer so we can avoid scheduling high-entropy tenants to same host during rollout (product + infra). Owner: Ravi Patel. ETA: 3 weeks.
- Add a dynconfig flag to reduce prefetch aggressiveness per-tenant. Owner: Sofia Garcia. ETA: 1 week.

Longer-term design changes (postmortem candidates):
- Rework index data structure to support lock-free incremental rehash to avoid full-host rehash pauses. (Research/Applied-ML + Serving Runtime).
- Shard index by tenant group to minimize cross-tenant amplification. Need capacity analysis.
- Smarter eviction smoothing algorithm that factors in index entropy and recent rehash events when computing target eviction rate.

Open questions / unknowns (notes-to-self):
- Is high index_entropy always bad, or does it reflect valid high-cardinality workloads that we should accept but route differently?
- Do certain model prompt patterns (e.g., long-form code completions) produce consistent hotkey signatures?
- How much operator burden will tenant-aware sharding add?

Immediate next steps (for oncall):
- If alerted: run triage checklist and apply one short-term mitigation (reduce prefetch, increase eviction smoothing).
- After incident: annotate the timeline in the incident channel with index_entropy screenshots and hotkey samples.
- Create follow-up Jira tickets for the short-term fixes above and prioritize in next SRE planning sprint.

Notes / random observations from debugging sessions:
- We observed one host where index_entropy oscillated with an exact 90s period; that corresponded to a background compaction job default interval.
- In at least two incidents, the batch collector's lock stack traces showed contention on 'bucket_map' mutex while eviction was in-flight -> indicates lock coupling problem.

Appendix: quick-scan checklist for pager (one-liner steps)
- Check grafana 'KV index entropy' panel -> if >0.5 proceed.
- Run hotkey capture on host.
- If single tenant dominates -> throttle/rollback.
- Otherwise: apply eviction smoothing + disable prefetch for tenant group.
- Monitor p99 and eviction_rate for 5m; if no improvement take host out of rotation.

End of notes. This doc is intentionally informal — use it as a starting point for a formal runbook and a postmortem if we get a repeat incident.
